summary: Over the last 4 weeks training has been heavily swim and bike dominant with only one run logged (10km at 169bpm avg HR, a high-effort effort that signals running fitness is underdeveloped relative to race targets). Sleep is chronically short — the majority of nights fall below 300 minutes, with several dipping below 210 minutes — and body battery scores are consistently low, suggesting accumulated fatigue that could compromise race performance and injury resilience. The Half Oceanman 5km open-water swim is today (Oct 3), so the immediate priority shifts to the Treviso 10K in 8 days, for which the athlete needs a controlled mini-taper starting now.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — aim for 7+ hours nightly before the Treviso 10K; chronically short sleep (many nights under 4 hours) is the single biggest recovery limiter visible in the data.
For Treviso 10K (Oct 10), target 5:45/km conservatively given only one run in 4 weeks; start controlled and negative-split the back half rather than chasing the target pace from the gun.

Reintroduce running progressively after Treviso — the 169bpm avg HR on your only recent 10km run at 6:15/km pace indicates you are currently aerobically deconditioned for running; build gently with 2–3 easy runs per week before resuming intervals.

The Tuesday Oct 6 interval session (6×800m at 4:55–5:10/km) falls 4 days after today's 5km open-water race and 4 days before Treviso — this is too intense given both the residual swim fatigue and the pre-race taper window; replace with an easy shakeout.

Power data is missing on all outdoor rides — adding a power meter or regularly using the indoor trainer with ERG mode would allow much more precise Z2 compliance and remove the guesswork from your Ironman bike build.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Evening session — 6×800m intervals at 4:55–5:10/km, 90 min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Easy 25–30 min shakeout jog at 6:30–7:00/km, flat, HR under 140bpm — no intervals
proposed_changes.reason: Running hard intervals 4 days after a 5km open-water race and 4 days before Treviso 10K is a textbook over-intensity error inside a taper window; easy movement aids recovery without digging a deeper hole.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip — full rest or 20-min gentle walk only
proposed_changes.reason: Swimming the day of today's Half Oceanman race and then returning to the pool 3 days later adds unnecessary fatigue in the Treviso taper window; the body needs absorption time, not another swim load.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Evening session — Z2 maintenance spin 128–177W, 45–60 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 20–25 min very easy spin below 128W (Z1 recovery only), cadence drills, no tempo effort
proposed_changes.reason: Two days before Treviso 10K the legs need to feel light; even a gentle Z2 spin accumulates residual fatigue that can blunt race-day sharpness for an athlete with limited recent run volume.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Gym / Strength — 40–50 min full strength session
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip gym session entirely — substitute 10 min of light mobility and leg swings only
proposed_changes.reason: Strength training induces 24–48hr muscular fatigue; performing it 2 days before a 10K race on an already under-run athlete significantly increases injury risk and reduces race-day leg freshness.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk17 Evening session — Z2 maintenance spin 128–177W, 45–60 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Easy 30–35 min run at 6:30–7:00/km (conversational pace, HR under 145bpm) to begin re-establishing running frequency post-Treviso
proposed_changes.reason: With only one run logged in 4 weeks and a marathon 127 days away, replacing one weekly bike maintenance spin with an easy aerobic run accelerates the necessary shift toward higher run frequency without adding overall load.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap at 12–13km at 6:30–6:45/km (strictly aerobic, conversational effort, no negative-split attempt)
proposed_changes.reason: Given only one run in the last 4 weeks at a high HR, jumping straight to a 17.6km long run after Treviso 10K the previous weekend risks injury and excessive soreness; a reduced but consistent long run restarts the running base safely.
